kW is power: how much is being used right now. kWh is energy: power over time. A 1 kW heater running for 3 hours uses 3 kWh.
Peak demand is the most power drawn at a single moment, for example when the AC, well pump and oven all start together. Batteries and inverters must be sized for it.
A demand charge is a monthly fee for each kW of your single highest peak, on top of the energy you use. Shaving that one peak lowers the whole charge.
Islanding means the microgrid disconnects from the utility during an outage and keeps running on its own sources, then reconnects when the grid is back.
Standard utility reliability scores (IEEE 1366). SAIFI: how often the average customer loses power. SAIDI: total minutes out per year. CAIDI: how long each outage lasts.
Duration is how many hours the battery can deliver its full power. A 4 MW battery with 4 hours of duration stores 16 MWh.
